scope: Real model tool call + MCP stdio protocol. The live runtime->Gateway->Main correlation leg is NOT yet demonstrated.

mcpProtocol.transport: real stdio against the built CLI (vb mcp)
mcpProtocol.cancel: tools/call + notifications/cancelled sent on the same connection
mcpProtocol.conclusion: failure is never degraded to isError=false; the advertised list is filtered by the active driver

fix.problem: vb mcp exited immediately: the CLI deliberate post-command flush termination ran right after startMcpServer connected the stdio transport, so initialize/tools-list/tools-call never happened. The whole MCP surface was dead.
fix.change: packages/versebrowser/src/cli.ts keeps the MCP process alive after startMcpServer (await a never-resolving promise), applied through the sanctioned integration patch because src/cli.ts is a hash-pinned import.
fix.verified: module/host-integration/api-coverage verify pass (the manifest pins the patched hash); the MCP probe passes after the patch and timed out before it.

gap.detail: The model->Gateway->Main->driver correlation leg (requestId/toolCallId/session/owner/event) still needs a runtime-side run: the renderer gateway.rpc surface is intentionally read-only for mutations, so a probe cannot drive agentBrowser.invoke from the renderer.
gap.nextStep: fix the provider-injection gap (why an account created via providers.createAccount + agents.updateModel does not reach the runtime's provider resolution), then re-run the control spec; once the control passes, N7's live leg can assert the correlation.
gap.notBlockedOnOwner: the local endpoint is live (127.0.0.1:3065); no owner action is needed for the next step.

liveAttempt.result: The live chain now reaches a REAL model tool call: with the real local endpoint the runtime records assistant toolCall entries for agent_browser carrying call ids (call_bb62b56ad73a43768051895c, call_0771c867f9eb4e8e93d58e01). It stops before Main because the endpoint returns malformed tool arguments (the string is missing its opening brace), which the runtime correctly rejects.
liveAttempt.providerLimitation: glm-5.3-flash returns arguments: {} for the tool call regardless of the prompt; hy3 does not call the tool at all
harnessFixes: local (ignored) node_modules/electron dist + path.txt pointing at the frozen Electron 40.8.4
spec uses launchElectronApp with skipSetup and the DERIVED runtime provider key (custom-livee2ec), not the bare vendor id

providerRootCause.detail: the resident endpoint's tool-call argument assembly drops the first chunk
providerRootCause.observed: the arguments string arrives without its leading brace
providerRootCause.effect: runtime JSON parse yields {} -> 'action: must have required properties action'

stubAttempt.detail: a labelled in-spec protocol stub returning a well-formed OpenAI Responses function_call was added, and the stub logs every incoming request. It received ZERO requests in two runs (stub-key and real-looking key), so the E2E run is not actually routed to the injected endpoint - it most likely uses the machine's own configured provider.
stubAttempt.impact: this means the observed empty tool arguments cannot yet be attributed to the injected endpoint from the E2E; only the DIRECT call to 127.0.0.1:3065 (recorded earlier) proves that endpoint's malformed arguments.
stubAttempt.honestyFix: the E2E assertion originally matched the tool name anywhere in the history, which the PROMPT text satisfied; it now requires an actual toolCall entry, so the current stub runs correctly FAIL.

isolationFinding.detail: the in-test protocol stub logged ZERO incoming requests across three runs (stub key, real-looking key, and with apiProtocol=openai-responses on an ephemeral base URL). The provider account IS created with that base URL and the model ref IS updated, yet the runtime never calls it - so the app provider store is not the source the runtime uses for the model call (the runtime resolves providers from its own openclaw config).
isolationFinding.consequence: every live run so far therefore used the machine's own configured provider. The agent_browser toolCall with a real call id is still real model evidence, but it is NOT evidence about the injected endpoint, and the empty arguments cannot be attributed to that endpoint.
isolationFinding.codeChange: the spec now forwards CLAWX_LIVE_API_PROTOCOL into the provider account (a real gap: custom endpoints need the protocol set).
isolationFinding.status: open - needs the runtime-side provider resolution instrumented

controlExperiment.detail: the repository's own live-model spec (chat-cache-live-model.spec.ts) fails identically against the same endpoint: no assistant message within 180s. So provider injection is broken repo-wide in this checkout, not just in the N7 spec.
controlExperiment.implication: live runs here are not attributable to an injected endpoint; fixing the provider injection is a prerequisite for N7's live leg.
